payout_quote: Official GreenPal vendor handbook: 'So for example if you win a new customer at $50 per mowing... Customer payment: $50.00 / GreenPal Platform Fee: $2.50 / Estimated Stripe processing fee: $1.75 / Estimated Vendor balance: $45.75.' Also: 'It's totally free to bid... bid often and bid fast as they usually pick the first price they like.' Customer payments go through your connected Stripe account.
timing: Paid through your own Stripe account after job completion; Stripe controls payout schedule (typically ~2 business days to bank).
eligibility: Appropriate skills/licenses to operate a lawn-care business
Smartphone for bids, job photos, and customer texts
steps: Sign up as a GreenPal vendor and connect your Stripe account
Bid fast on lawns near you (free to bid; first good price usually wins)
Win the job and complete the mow + edge + blow
Upload a photo of the completed work to trigger payment
Customer payment flows to your Stripe, minus 5% GreenPal fee and Stripe processing
catches: 5% GreenPal platform fee + ~2.9% + $0.30 Stripe fee on every job
You set the price — bid too high and you lose; too low and you work for nothing
Equipment, gas, and maintenance are entirely yours
First mow is an 'audition' — no recurring revenue until the customer rebooks
Seasonal: demand dies in winter in most markets
biggest_catch: You set your own bid, so the $50 example is just math — in competitive neighborhoods vendors undercut each other, and after the 5% + Stripe fees plus your gas and equipment, the margin on a cheap bid is thin.
upfront_fee: $0 to bid; equipment and Stripe setup are worker-provided.
notes: Official vendor handbook gives the exact $50 mow fee breakdown ($45.75 vendor balance). Range $30-$75 per typical single mow. Timing via own Stripe account (~2 business days) — 'days' speed.

repeatable.cadence: Bid fast, win the lawn, complete the mow, upload the photo to trigger payment — and convert first mows into weekly repeat customers so the loop runs itself.

maximize: Bid within minutes of a job posting — GreenPal's own handbook says the first good price usually wins; price tight but never below your gas+time floor; convert every first mow into a recurring weekly customer (that's where the real money is); stack jobs by neighborhood to cut drive time; upsell hedge trimming and leaf cleanup in-app; photo-document every finished lawn to get paid without disputes.
who_pays: The customer pays you directly — their payment flows into your own connected Stripe account, with GreenPal taking a 5% platform fee (plus Stripe's processing fee). GreenPal never holds your pay.
who_qualifies: You need your own lawn-care equipment (mower, edger, blower), the skills or licenses to run a lawn-care business, a connected Stripe account for payouts, and a smartphone for bidding, job photos, and customer texts.
work_available: You bid on lawns near you and it's free to bid — but the first good price usually wins, so expect bidding wars in competitive neighborhoods. Also seasonal: demand dies in winter in most markets.
what_gets_accepted: You get paid when you complete the mow and upload a photo of the finished lawn — the photo is what triggers payment, so document every job. Win the first mow and the real money comes from customers rebooking you weekly. GreenPal's specific removal policy is not publicly stated.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Bidding is officially free, but everything else is yours: mower, edger, blower, gas, and maintenance — plus the 5% GreenPal fee and about 2.9% + $0.30 Stripe fee on every job. On a $50 mow the official breakdown leaves you $45.75 before gas and equipment. Unpaid time: bidding, driving between lawns, and first mows that don't convert to repeat customers.
when_cash_arrives: Customer payments go to your Stripe account after you complete the job and upload the photo; Stripe's standard schedule then applies — typically about 2 business days to your bank.
